question: Is Machine-wide Cargo Cache V3 complete, technically correct, safely migratable, enforceable across normal Cargo entry points, & sufficient to prevent internal-disk or unbounded external-cache recurrence?
constraints: All meaningful Rust/Cargo payload lives on external APFS volume D.
D is resolved & verified by volume UUID; no silent internal fallback.
New Cargo projects require zero per-project cache setup.
Active builds, published artifacts, source, product assets, & durable evidence must not be lost.
Unrelated workspaces must not share one raw Cargo target.

Plan must address debug, release, test, bench, doc, install, Tauri, IDE, agents, worktrees, temp, Cargo home, rustup, sccache, local target, .cache targets, legacy release cache, migration, GC, UX, & observability.
Round one pass means fresh verdict outcome SUPPORTED with no unresolved critical/high in-scope defect.
invariants: Cache mutation is lease-aware, path-contained, same-volume, auditable, & recoverable through quarantine.
Every managed entry has ownership, lifecycle, budget, & retention.
Build admission preserves 220 GiB hard free-space floor & prunes toward 300 GiB.
Shared cross-workspace reuse occurs through sccache/Cargo home, not shared raw target.
Direct bypasses are rejected or forced external within supported machine execution surfaces.
nonGoals: Changing application product behavior unrelated to build/cache storage.
Treating signed installers or durable evidence as disposable cache.
Guaranteeing policy against a malicious administrator intentionally invoking arbitrary binaries with scrubbed environment.
embeddedEvidence:
PLAN_SHA256=ee378e5dd4f4634499b76af7cdd90baea6603b3a19e8f5981f134ba25aceaf47\n# Machine-wide Cargo Cache V3

Status: Covenant review candidate v2
Scope: this Mac, every current or future Cargo workspace, external storage only

## Outcome

Every Cargo invocation launched through supported machine development surfaces uses external D storage, isolated target state, shared compiler/dependency caches, complete lifecycle metadata, bounded garbage collection, & fail-closed behavior when D is unavailable. Supported surfaces are interactive login shells, Codex/Claude tools, launchd jobs, VS Code/Rust Analyzer, Tauri/npm/pnpm scripts, RightKit release, workspace hooks, & registered IDE/task-runner integrations. No payload from those surfaces may fall back internally. Intentional administrator bypass through an absolute toolchain binary with scrubbed environment remains outside enforcement scope & must be named as unsupported by doctor/audit.

## External root

Resolve D by APFS volume UUID, then use `<mount>/.rightsuite/`:

```text
.rightsuite/
  bin/
  runtime/
  toolchains/rustup/
  cargo-home/{bin,registry,git}/
  cache/
    sccache/
    targets/{dev,test,release,worktree}/
    scratch/
    recovery/
    quarantine/
  state/{registry.sqlite,leases,gc,receipts}/
  logs/
```

Internal disk retains only APFS UUID locator, launchd definition, & shell bootstrap, below 1 MB total.

## Machine environment

Login/bootstrap reads only expected APFS UUID + relative root from internal locator. It enumerates mounted APFS volumes, selects matching UUID, captures mount device, canonicalizes mountpoint, verifies writable external media, then exports `RIGHTSUITE_STORAGE_ROOT`, `RIGHT_RELEASE_CACHE_ROOT`, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `SCCACHE_DIR`, plus external shim path before every Cargo/Rust path. It must never call `mkdir` on configured mount path before UUID/device verification. Apply to interactive shells, launchd jobs, Codex/Claude agents, VS Code/Rust Analyzer, Tauri/npm/pnpm scripts, & workspace hooks. Wrong-volume same-name mount or missing UUID fails before any path creation.

Bootstrap order is fixed: resolve UUID → verify device/mount → locate already-installed external runtime → construct environment → run doctor → permit Cargo. Toolchain installation/update follows same resolver. Current Cargo version must pass setup probes for configured environment variables & `build.build-dir`; unsupported toolchains are rejected before adoption.

## Cargo guard

Install immutable/versioned RightKit cache runtime under external root. External `cargo` shim invokes `right-cache cargo`; runtime invokes actual toolchain Cargo through `rustup which cargo` without recursion.

For every invocation, storage enforcement runs before light/heavy classification:

1. Verify configured volume UUID is mounted.
2. Find workspace root from `--manifest-path` or nearest `Cargo.toml`.
3. Canonicalize workspace path.
4. Resolve rustc commit, host triple, command class, & worktree state.
5. Key target by SHA-256 of canonical workspace path + rustc commit + host triple.
6. Select `cache/targets/<class>/<workspace>-<key>`.
7. Overwrite `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, `SCCACHE_DIR`, `CARGO_HOME/config.toml` location, & Cargo-child `TMPDIR` with UUID-verified managed external paths.
8. Acquire per-entry lease/build lock.
9. Run real Cargo.
10. Record result, size, last use, & command class.
11. Release lease.
12. Run bounded post-build GC.

`cargo new/init/fmt/metadata/tree/fetch` receive external home/temp/wrapper policy before skipping heavy-work admission. In particular `fetch` must write registry/Git data only to external Cargo home. Any command capable of creating build output also receives guard-owned explicit `--target-dir <registered-entry>` after caller override validation.

## Classes & retention

| Operation | Class | Retention |
|---|---|---|
| build/check/run/clippy/fix/doc | dev | 7 idle days |
| test/nextest/bench | test | 24 idle hours |
| RightKit release | release | latest successful target per app |
| Git worktree | worktree | 48 idle hours |
| install/probe/temp manifest | scratch | remove after success; 6-hour crash TTL |
| interrupted migration | recovery | 48 hours |

All debug, release, incremental, deps, build scripts, examples, docs, package output, timings, integration-test temporary data, & local native intermediates live inside registered entries. Unrelated workspaces never share raw Cargo target directories; safe cross-workspace reuse comes from sccache + shared Cargo dependency/source cache.

## Bypass prevention

Guard rejects every caller `--target-dir`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR`, `SCCACHE_DIR`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, `CARGO_HOME`, or `RUSTUP_HOME` override unless it exactly matches UUID-verified registered state. It strips caller target routing & injects guard-owned explicit `--target-dir <registered-entry>` for build-capable commands. RightKit release receives short-lived scoped ownership token bound to request digest, registry entry, process identity, & expiry.

Cargo configuration precedence is explicit: setup owns external `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`; guard discovers every `.cargo/config`/`.cargo/config.toml` from workspace to filesystem root plus each `--config` file/value. It TOML-parses inputs & rejects storage/compiler-wrapper keys including `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`, relevant `[env]` overrides, or aliases that invoke absolute Cargo/rustup. Safe non-storage config keys remain allowed. Parsing ambiguity, duplicate legacy/config.toml precedence, unreadable config, or unsupported Cargo version fails closed. Tests freeze Cargo precedence behavior for supported versions.

Managed `rustup` shim prevents `rustup run <toolchain> cargo` bypass from supported PATH surfaces. IDE/task-runner configuration receives external homes + shim path explicitly, not through assumed shell inheritance. Global external Cargo config supplies external workspace-hashed `build-dir` + sccache as defense-in-depth for direct actual Cargo with inherited managed environment. Static repo audit rejects absolute toolchain Cargo/rustup paths. Doctor reports any visible unguarded Cargo/rustup executable ahead of shims & any registered integration lacking environment proof.

## Registry & concurrency

Each cache entry records schema, ID, canonical workspace path/hash, class, toolchain, triple, created/last-used/last-success/last-failure times, measured size, lease identity including PID + OS process-start token + executable identity, retention, pinned state, & rebuildable state. Every guarded command uses durable registry + per-entry lock; same-entry builds serialize. Lease acquisition precedes target directory creation; release runs in `finally`; stale recovery requires PID/start-token mismatch. Distinct targets may run within machine heavy-work policy. GC revalidates source revision, marker, physical containment, volume UUID/device, lease, PID start identity, & registry transaction before mutation.

## Budgets

| Class | Budget |
|---|---:|
| Cargo registry/Git cache | 24 GiB |
| sccache | 32 GiB |
| dev targets | 72 GiB |
| test/bench targets | 24 GiB |
| release targets | 24 GiB |
| scratch/install | 8 GiB |
| recovery | 8 GiB |
| total | 192 GiB |

Desired D free space is 300 GiB; build hard floor is 220 GiB. Before heavy work, GC prunes toward 300 GiB. If safe reclamation cannot preserve 220 GiB plus predicted build growth, build fails before writes. No internal fallback. Initial class budgets are provisional policy defaults: migration captures baseline, 72-hour soak measures peak/working-set/P95 growth, & final budgets require explicit receipt while total cap + free-space floors remain invariant.

## GC

Prune crashed scratch, expired tests, expired worktrees, stale recovery, superseded release targets, idle dev targets by LRU, sccache LRU, then Cargo registry/Git cache. Never prune active lease, pinned entry, current release target, current/previous signed artifact, or irreplaceable evidence.

Deletion acquires global GC lock + registry transaction, validates target twice, atomically renames entry into same-volume quarantine, commits quarantine receipt, deletes asynchronously, remeasures filesystem free bytes, & commits reclaimed-byte result. Unreadable paths, traversal errors, size errors, marker mismatch, registry disagreement, or volume-identity uncertainty are hard doctor/GC failures—never counted as zero or skipped. Run before/after heavy work, after interruption, at login, every 30 minutes via LaunchAgent, at watermark crossing, & manually.

Unknown directories inside managed root fail doctor instead of being ignored. Reconciliation detects missing entries, unmarked directories, dead leases, duplicate targets, path escapes, size drift, & wrong-volume mounts.

## Local-target prevention

First Cargo use automatically registers any new workspace. Scoped audit rejects real `target/`, `src-tauri/target` except owned link, `.cache/cargo-target`, `.cache/*target*`, legacy `.right-release/cache`, legacy target backups, or custom target roots. New scaffolds receive `target/` + `.cache/` ignores. Pre-build/post-build workspace audit plus scheduled registered-workspace audit prevent recurrence.

## Artifact boundary

Signed/published installers are artifacts, not cache. Retain locally current + one rollback artifact; GitHub Releases remains durable publication. Models/product assets require explicit manifest classification. Benchmark evidence is retained only when referenced by a durable evidence manifest. Everything else build-derived is rebuildable cache.

## Migration

Stop active Cargo/RightKit work, verify no live compiler/process-start token, inventory every source path into immutable classification manifest, classify preserved artifacts/evidence, then same-volume rename targets/backups into recovery quarantine without duplicate copies. A moved cache never becomes active directly: validate marker, toolchain, workspace identity, containment, & registry schema first; only then atomically activate. Invalid/stale material remains quarantined. Migrate active Rust toolchains, Cargo registry/Git cache, sccache, valid release targets, & installed Cargo binaries into unified root. Quarantine CodeRight, Membrane, HeardRight, CutRight, ViewRight, worktree, dispatch, `.build-home/tmp`, `.cache/cargo-target`, legacy `.right-release`, dated Cargo/cache backup build outputs. Write idempotent prepare/move/validate/activate/expire receipt per path. Verify all suites before quarantine expiry; rollback reverses only validated same-volume renames from receipt.

## Product & diagnostics

Expose `right-cache status|doctor|audit|prune|migrate|explain|cargo`. RightKit Hub displays category usage, active leases, watermarks, unmanaged paths, reclaimable bytes, last GC, migration state, & safe prune control.

Workspace doctor fails unless volume identity before path creation, shim precedence, direct rustup/Cargo visibility, real Cargo separation, external toolchains/home/cache/temp/build-dir, supported Cargo feature probes, config-precedence scan, integration environment proofs, sccache cap, scheduler, registry, leases/PID-start tokens, local-target audit, RightKit version parity, budget, & free-space watermark pass.

## Rollout

1. Freeze Cache V3 schema, ADR, threat model, & failing tests.
2. Build storage resolver, registry, lease model, GC, cargo/rustup shims, & doctor.
3. Integrate RightKit release target bridge + release retention.
4. Install external runtime, environment bootstrap, LaunchAgent, IDE/agent configuration.
5. Migrate existing cache/toolchains without duplication.
6. Publish breaking RightKit release & update every suite app together.
7. Run focused, contract, light-command storage, Cargo-config precedence, absolute-path/static-audit, concurrency, PID reuse, interruption, unreadable-directory, low-space, no-volume, wrong-volume, Tauri, IDE, delegated-agent, migration-resume, & security tests.
8. Run 72-hour soak with zero unmanaged targets & cache within cap.

## Acceptance

- `command -v cargo` resolves external RightKit guard.
- Fresh project needs no manual cache setup & creates no local target.
- Full suite build writes no Cargo payload internally.
- Missing/wrong D fails before writes.
- Every supported-surface override/bypass route is rejected or forced external; doctor enumerates unsupported direct absolute binaries explicitly.
- `cargo fetch`, metadata, fmt, init/new & every light command inherit external Cargo/Rustup/temp policy.
- Cargo config precedence tests prove no project or CLI config can redirect build/cache writes.
- Concurrent same-workspace builds serialize under PID-start-aware lease.
- Active entries survive GC; dead leases recover safely.
- All app-local/legacy targets are gone.
- All apps use same current RightKit cache contract.
- Scheduled GC has current successful receipt.
- Managed cache stays at or below 192 GiB.
- D returns to at least 300 GiB free after migration/prune.
- Hub & doctor report zero unmanaged namespaces.

MEASURED_STATE: D was 98% full with 27.5 GB free. RightKit root held ~244 GiB; unmanaged dev-targets alone held ~166 GiB. Documented prune returned one empty candidate & reclaimed 0. Local targets included CodeRight ~88 GiB, Membrane ~49 GiB, HeardRight >100 GiB, CutRight ~18 GiB, ViewRight ~7 GiB. Cargo guard existed at /Users/adrdsouza/bin/cargo but PATH resolved dated /Volumes/D/adrdsouza-cargo-home-20260726/bin/cargo first. Cleanup raised D free space to ~200 GiB.

ROUND_1_SYNTHESIS: REVISE. Critical gaps accepted: UUID verification must precede mkdir; all light commands must receive external homes/temp; Cargo/rustup direct-path boundary must be explicit; caller target/config overrides need authoritative precedence handling; every target needs registry/lease; GC must cover all classes with quarantine/receipts/hard errors; leases need PID start identity; migration requires staged quarantine validation before activation.
knownUnknowns: Exact compatibility & operational value of Cargo build.build-dir path templating across all scripts.
Every IDE/helper that invokes absolute rustup or toolchain Cargo outside managed PATH.
Measured steady-state cache working set needed by largest suite builds.
Which benchmark/model/evidence directories are durable artifacts versus rebuildable cache.
Whether 300 GiB free watermark remains compatible with non-cache product data growth.
knownWeaknesses: Any administrator can intentionally bypass user-space wrapper with direct binary + scrubbed environment.
Budget values are initial policy estimates, not yet derived from 72-hour telemetry.
Scheduled 30-minute audit is not instantaneous for non-wrapper writers.
Global external Cargo config is defense-in-depth, not dynamic target namespacing by itself.
alternativesConsidered: One global raw CARGO_TARGET_DIR: rejected for workspace collisions, lock contention, & unsafe coupling.
Per-project targets only: rejected for unbounded duplication.
Only sccache: rejected because target/debug/incremental/test outputs remain unbounded.
Only scheduled cleanup: rejected because bypass can fill disk between sweeps.
Internal toolchains with external targets: rejected because internal disk is 256 GB & requirement is external-only payload.
requestedOutcome: SUPPORTED only if plan is implementable & sufficient without unresolved critical/high in-scope defect; otherwise REVISE with exact finding, failure path, affected decision/acceptance, & recommended amendment.

lensRequirements: Adversarial enforcement, operations, UX & future-project coverage
